title: The Roost & Sprout Village Café
rules: Espresso extraction follows strict physical principles where dry dose, grind fineness, water temperature, and liquid yield govern flavor balance; under-extraction causes sourness while over-extraction causes harsh bitterness [1, 2, 3, 4].
Steaming milk creates microfoam via protein stabilization and lactose solubilization, but milk must never exceed 65°C–70°C to avoid scalding whey proteins and burning sugars [5, 6].
Steam wands must be purged and wiped immediately after every pitcher, and dairy and plant-milk allergens must use strictly segregated pitchers and cloths to prevent cross-contact [5, 7].
Espresso crema and microfoam emulsion decay rapidly after extraction, requiring beverages to be served within minutes of preparation [5, 8].
